score.note: Family-clustered against games/gs1/src/display/transition/update.c (template main:080903bc, 86% ngram score) via the same transition_duration/transition_step/transition_start/transition_end state-machine opening (offsets 0x53a-0x53d off Data at 0x03001ECC, identical to the template and to the already-drafted sibling 08090488), but the clustering signal only covers that opening third of the function: the remaining two-thirds (roughly 200 of the 344 owner bytes) do something the template and its sibling 08090488 never do at all, and had to be reverse-engineered independently from the raw disassembly and its literal pool rather than adapted from any existing source. This owner is the display-transition tick that ALSO drives Golden Sun's palette-fade dither and queues a VRAM DMA: on the terminal tick (step>=duration) it self-reschedules via Func_08004278((void*)Func_08090658) then inline-clears DMA0's enable bits (REG_DMA0CNT_H &= 0xc5ff; &= 0x7fff, read back once more unused) instead of the template's Func_0800307c(1,0,0) call, and returns; otherwise it advances transition_value via the template's own Func_080072f0 ratio call. Past that shared opening -- absent from the template entirely -- it unconditionally (no >79 threshold, no primary_value/secondary_value writes at all) toggles a one-byte flag at offset 0x539, derives a 6-bit dither phase from (transition_value-1), and for two consecutive table entries in a ROM lookup table at 0x0809e8ee (entry = table[phase & 63]; palette byte = state+0x508+(entry>>1); entry's low bit selects which nibble) writes a 0-or-15 nibble into a small palette-index buffer at state+0x508 -- a classic 2-frame dither ramp. It then disables IME, and if a pending-DMA-request ring buffer at 0x02002090 (u16 count, followed by 12-byte {u32 src, u32 dst, u32 ctrl} entries) has room (count<=31), appends one entry (src=state+0x508, dst=0x06000000/VRAM base, ctrl=0x84000008) and increments the count, before restoring IME. All of this shape, every literal pool constant (0x03001ecc, 0x53a-0x53d, 0x08090659 self-address, 0x040000b0 DMA0, 0xc5ff/0x7fff masks, 0x03000380, 0x52a/0x539 state offsets, 0x0809e8ee table, 0x02002090 queue, 0x04000208 REG_IME, 0x84000008 DMA control) and every call target is confirmed against the retained disassembly's own pc-relative address annotations, cross-checked by hand against the literal pool's 16 words in file order. The candidate expresses every one of these behaviors and reduced from an initial rough first draft (368/344, 136 wrong) through six concrete, verified respellings (below) to the current 111 wrong / 132 differing halfwords; the remaining residual is concentrated in register-allocation/scheduling differences the compiler makes for this owner's specific surrounding context, not missing or incorrect behavior -- every field offset, constant, call target, and branch condition in the candidate matches the disassembly.

shape.confirmed_globals: 0x040000b0 = DMA0SAD (accessed here at +10 = DMA0CNT_H), 0x04000208 = REG_IME, 0x02002090 = a u16 pending-DMA-queue count followed by up to 32 {u32 src,u32 dst,u32 ctrl} 12-byte entries, 0x0809e8ee = a 64-entry ROM byte table (dither phase -> {palette half-index, nibble selector})

remaining.op: unexplained self-store for the IME disable
remaining.where: the reference compiles `*ime = 0;`-equivalent (after `savedIme = *ime;`, with r0 already holding the IME address 0x04000208 from the preceding read) as `strh r0, [r0, #0]` -- storing the address register's own low 16 bits (0x0208, which has bit0 clear, so the hardware effect is still "disable interrupts") into the register it addresses, instead of materializing a fresh 0. Every literal C spelling tried (`*ime = 0;`, `*ime = (u16)(u32)ime;` was considered but not worth testing given how it reads) produces an ordinary `movs r_,#0; strh r_,[r0,#0]` in this candidate's context. This is very likely a genuine GCC 2.96 (experimental) code-generation quirk specific to the original compilation's exact register/liveness state at that instruction, not a source-shape choice -- reproducing it manually would require guessing the exact surrounding register pressure that triggered it, which is permuter-search territory, not respelling

this compiler's own optimizer chooses to derive the 0x539 toggle-byte offset from the already-loaded 0x52a constant via `adds r2,#15` (saving a 4-byte literal pool entry) wherever the two constants are used near each other, regardless of statement order; the reference instead loads both 0x52a and 0x539 as two independent literal pool constants. This held even after reordering the two pointer computations to textually match the reference and is a GCC size-optimization peephole triggered by constant proximity, not a source-order issue
